relationship.statement: A pendulum's swing period increases with string length and decreases with stronger gravity, while bob mass has no effect. Release angle sets swing width and max speed, and only slightly lengthens period at large angles.
assumptions: The string is massless and inextensible, with all bob mass at a single point.
Air drag and pivot friction are zero, so total mechanical energy stays constant.
The period formula uses the small-angle approximation (release angles under 15 deg).

quantities.label: String length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the fixed pivot point to the center of the pendulum bob.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the bob; scales gravitational force and inertia equally so period is unchanged.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle measured from straight down where the bob is released from rest.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational acceleration acting on the pendulum bob.

quantities.label: Air drag
quantities.meaning: Friction and air resistance opposing motion, fixed at zero in this ideal model.

quantities.label: Period
quantities.meaning: Time required for one complete back-and-forth swing cycle.

quantities.label: Frequency
quantities.meaning: Number of complete swing cycles completed per second (1/T).

quantities.label: Swing angle
quantities.meaning: Instantaneous angle of the string from the vertical equilibrium line.

quantities.label: Max speed
quantities.meaning: Peak speed of the bob as it passes through the lowest point.

quantities.label: Total energy
quantities.meaning: Conserved mechanical energy of the swing, proportional to bob mass.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var L = 2.0; var m = 1.0; var g = inputs.g; var theta0 = inputs.theta0; var rad0 = theta0 * Math.PI / 180; var T = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(L / g); var f = 1 / T; var omega = 2 * Math.PI * f; var theta = theta0 * Math.cos(omega * t); var thetaRad = theta * Math.PI / 180; var bob_x = L * Math.sin(thetaRad); var bob_y = L - L * Math.cos(thetaRad); var E_total = m * g * L * (1 - Math.cos(rad0)); var v_max = Math.sqrt(2 * E_total / m); var g_tip_y = 1.6 - 0.05 * g; return { T: T, f: f, theta: theta, v_max: v_max, E_total: E_total, bob_x: bob_x, bob_y: bob_y, g_tip_y: g_tip_y, is_large_angle: theta0 > 15, is_high_gravity: g > 12, is_low_gravity: g < 7 }; }

outputs.meaning: Time for one full swing cycle in the small-angle model.
Instantaneous angle of the string from vertical.
Peak speed of the bob at the lowest point.
Total conserved mechanical energy of the pendulum.
Horizontal position of the bob relative to the vertical line.
Vertical height of the bob above the lowest point.
Tip y-coordinate of the gravity indicator arrow.
True when release angle exceeds 15 degrees.
True when gravity is stronger than 12 m/s^2.
True when gravity is weaker than 7 m/s^2.

always: Fixed: L = 2.0 m, mass m = 1.0 kg.
Period T depends on L and g, not m.

cases.text: Wide angle boosts speed and energy.
Stronger g shortens swing period T.
Weaker g lengthens swing period T.

lesson.title: What changes a pendulum swing?
lesson.description: Watch a pendulum swing with fixed string length and bob mass while a graph traces its angle over time. Change release angle and gravity to see what alters period, speed, and energy.
lesson.instructions: Drag Release angle to change swing width while keeping string length and mass fixed, then adjust Gravity to speed up or slow down the cycle. Pause or scrub time to inspect the angle curve and live readouts.
lesson.goal: Gravity controls how fast a pendulum ticks, while release angle sets its swing width, peak speed, and total energy without changing its small-angle period.
